# INVESTMENT MEMORANDUM

**SESI, L.L.C. - First Amendment and Waiver to Credit Agreement**

---

## 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

**Date of Agreement:** May 13, 2021

**Borrower/Company Overview:** SESI, L.L.C., a Delaware limited liability company, with SESI Holdings, Inc. (Delaware corporation) as Parent, along with multiple subsidiary guarantors including Superior Energy Services, L.L.C. and other energy services entities.

**Transaction Description:** First Amendment and Waiver to an existing Credit Agreement originally dated February 2, 2021. The transaction involves JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as Administrative Agent, with Bank of America, N.A. and Citibank, N.A. as participating lenders.

**Purpose of Financing:** The amendment serves to: (i) extend the deadline until June 1, 2021 for delivery of Q1 2021 financial statements (consolidated balance sheets and profit/loss statements of Superior Topco), (ii) waive compliance with certain covenant sections related to Superior TopCo's potential inability to file its Q1 2021 Form 10-Q with the SEC on time, and (iii) implement various technical amendments to the original Credit Agreement.

**Company Background:** Based on the subsidiary guarantor names, the borrower appears to be part of the Superior Energy Services organization, operating in the energy services sector with various specialized subsidiaries including drilling, well control, inspection services, and energy equipment rental operations.

---

## 2. INVESTMENT HIGHLIGHTS & RISKS

### Key Strengths/Credit Positives:
• **Established lending relationship** with high-quality financial institutions (JPMorgan Chase as Administrative Agent, Bank of America, Citibank)
• **Cooperative borrower behavior** - proactively communicating potential compliance issues and seeking amendments rather than allowing defaults
• **Comprehensive guarantee structure** with multiple subsidiary guarantors providing credit enhancement
• **Diversified energy services platform** across multiple operational verticals based on guarantor entity names

### Principal Risks and Mitigating Factors:
• **Financial reporting delays** - Borrower experiencing difficulties meeting SEC reporting deadlines for Q1 2021, indicating potential operational or financial stress
• **Covenant compliance concerns** - Required waivers suggest the company may be operating near covenant boundaries
• **Energy sector exposure** - Operating in cyclical energy services industry subject to commodity price volatility
• **Limited financial transparency** - Amendment document does not provide visibility into underlying financial metrics or performance trends
